item.title: A need for Reformed traditions to transform towards a womanist turning point
item.description: The churches in post-1994 South Africa exist in a context of many challenges. This article will review literature from black and womanist perspectives to argue that Reformed traditions need to transform towards a womanist approach. This is because they collaborated to the socio-economic challenges of the post-1994 South Africa. item.title: The Trinity and cyber culture: Crafting theologically responsible analogies in the digital age
item.description: This article examines the use of cyber culture as a contemporary context for Trinitarian analogy within the discipline of systematic theology. Grounded in Scripture, the Nicene Creed, and classical Trinitarian doctrine, the study investigates whether and under what conditions phenomena such as algorithmic governance, digital identity, and online community may function as illustrative analogies without compromising doctrinal integrity. item.title: Is God enthroned upon the floods? (Ps 29:10) Religion and the climate change crisis in contemporary Ghana
item.description: Climate change has been identified as one of the most imminent threats to the survival of the human species. item.title: Performing gender equality: Internalising Bugis-Makassar cultural values (3S) as a theological strategy for transforming patriarchal structures
item.description: Gender inequality is a global problem and causes various acts of violence and suffering for women, especially in the third world, including Indonesia. item.title: Quantum Molinism: God’s fuzzy logic and the freedom to love

item.title: Balia, a Healing Tradition among the Kaili People of Indonesia: A Biblical Response
item.description: The Balia healing tradition remains a significant cultural and spiritual practice among the Kaili people of Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, including within Christian communities.
